8331: Family campground just north of Wiarton, a few minutes' walk from Berford Lake, under new owners, the Pletch family.  A shallow sandy beach with a boat launch, canoe, kayak and paddle-boat rentals, and horseshoes, karaoke, potlucks and fireworks.  Seasonal sites have a waiting list going into 2026. --Claude
8334: Municipality of Brockton campground on the Saugeen River at 20 Hannah Street in Walkerton, close to downtown: 16 full-service, 28 water-and-hydro and 31 unserviced sites plus 4 canoe sites, showers, a dump station, a playground, a dog park, a canoe and kayak launch and access to the multi-use trails.  Generators aren't allowed. --Claude
8342: Family-owned campground at 13685 ON-60 on Golden Lake, halfway between Barry's Bay and Renfrew, with 4,200 ft of waterfront: sites from unserviced to full hookups and pull-throughs, cabins, RV rentals and seasonal sites (C$2,100-3,300 a season plus tax and electricity).  Two beaches, a marina with a large dock and boat launch, a store, coin laundry and many events through the season. --Claude
9059: County of Grande Prairie campground where Pipestone Creek meets the Wapiti River, 16 km south of Wembley, near the world's largest Pachyrhinosaurus bone bed and the Philip J. Currie Dinosaur Museum.  There is no cell service.  Indoor showers and washrooms, a group day-use shelter, two playgrounds, a ball diamond, 7 km of hiking trails and boat access to the Wapiti; the trail to the bone bed is closed until further notice. --Claude
9074: Run by the Highwood Lions Club for the Town of High River in George Lane Memorial Park, beside the Highwood River among cottonwoods and within walking distance of downtown shopping and restaurants.  57 pull-through and back-in sites with 15- and 30-amp power, free showers, potable water, a free sani-dump and Wi-Fi, plus an overnight group site. --Claude
9139: Family-owned campground (Rainbow Beach Developments) beside the Pembina River gorge at Entwistle: 30 single sites, a tandem site and 10 group sites, with firewood included and a gated entrance.  The 2023 Parkland County wildfire left many of the single sites and trails with fewer trees; the group sites were untouched. --Claude
9602: Idaho Power park on the Idaho side of Oxbow Reservoir on the Snake River, 29 miles northwest of Cambridge on Idaho Highway 71: nine acres of grass and shade trees, 28 RV sites and 8 tent sites, a restroom with showers, a boat ramp and a camp host from early April to Labor Day.  Utility-run, so ownership is private. --Claude
9615: Idaho Power park on Hells Canyon Reservoir (Snake River), on Hells Canyon Road six miles downstream of Copperfield Park: 15 acres of lawns and shade trees, 21 RV sites with water and 30-amp power, 3 dry sites with power in the boat-ramp lot, 3 waterfront RV sites without hookups and 7 tent sites.  The road between Oxbow and Hells Canyon Dam sometimes closes; call 541-785-7251 for its status.  Utility-run, so ownership is private. --Claude
9722: Idaho Power park directly below C.J. Strike Dam, about 24 miles south of Mountain Home: 10 acres with 33 RV sites (shared water, no power), 3 turf tent sites, fire rings, a waterfront walking path, a seasonal dump station, a boat ramp and a reservable picnic shelter.  Camp hosts are on site Friday to Sunday from early April to Labor Day.  Utility-run, so ownership is private. --Claude
9723: Idaho Power park on 18 acres at the northwest corner of C.J. Strike Reservoir, about 23 miles south of Mountain Home: 30 RV sites (shared water, no power), 10 turf tent sites, a boat ramp and docks, a fish-cleaning station, a waterfront walking path and reservable picnic shelters.  Camp hosts are on site Friday to Sunday from early April to Labor Day.  Utility-run, so ownership is private. --Claude
9803: Kootenai County fairgrounds RV park at 482 E. Dalton Avenue in Coeur d'Alene, an easy drive or bike ride to the lake, mountain trails and shopping.  Full hookups at every site, pull-throughs on request, 3 tent sites, showers and Wi-Fi; a free public dump station is next door. --Claude
9805: Bonner County fairgrounds campground at 4203 N. Boyer Road in Sandpoint, close to Ponderay, Schweitzer and Lake Pend Oreille: 32 paved sites 12 ft wide and 27-48 ft long with 30/50-amp power and water, hot showers and restrooms, a covered pavilion, Wi-Fi and a camp host on site in season.  Tents aren't allowed on the grass. --Claude
9818: Idaho Power park on 12 acres at the Bruneau delta, on the south side of C.J. Strike Reservoir at the end of Cottonwood Road near milepost 72 of Idaho 78, about 26 miles south of Mountain Home: 33 sites for RVs or tents with shared water and no power, vault toilets, fire rings, a marina, a waterfront walking path and a reservable picnic shelter.  Camp hosts are on site Friday to Sunday from early April to Labor Day.  Utility-run, so ownership is private. --Claude
